Engineering signalling centres to trigger human trunk morphogenesis in vitro

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 37 min read (7350 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~37 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Vertebrate trunk development is orchestrated by endogenous signalling centres that generate gradients of signals such as WNT and BMP to pattern cell fates and drive morphogenesis1,2,3,4,5,6,7.
  • This is a preview of subscription content, access via your institution.
  • Access Nature and 54 other Nature Portfolio journals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Vertebrate trunk development is orchestrated by endogenous signalling centres that generate gradients of signals such as WNT and BMP to pattern cell fates and drive morphogenesis1,2,3,4,5,6,7. Whether these cues alone can reconstitute human trunk-like morphogenesis in vitro remains unknown. Here we present a synthetic embryology platform for high-throughput, spatiotemporal delivery of morphogen signals to epithelial cysts derived from human pluripotent stem cells. Transient WNT and BMP gradients are sufficient to drive the generation of axially elongating trunk-like structures that contain a central neural tube flanked by axial, paraxial, intermediate and lateral mesoderm. The geometry of the transient BMP signal exerts lasting control over mediolateral patterning and bilateral symmetry. Patterning and morphogenesis are sustained by neuromesodermal and lateral plate mesoderm progenitors induced by the initial cues, which act as endogenous signalling centres. Together, these findings define a minimal spatial code sufficient to reconstitute trunk-like morphogenesis in a human stem-cell-based model and establish a scalable platform for studying early human development and congenital disorders.

The scRNA-seq and bulk RNA-seq data generated for this study are available from the GEO under accessions GSE306808 and GSE347564, respectively. Sequencing reads were aligned to the GRCh38 human reference genome (10x Genomics GRCh38-2020 for scRNA-seq; Ensembl GRCh38, assembly accession GCA_000001405.29, for bulk RNA-seq). Previously published29 human embryo scRNA-seq data are available from the GEO under accession GSE155121. Other reanalysed datasets are available from the following repositories: mouse gastrulation, ArrayExpress (E-MTAB-6967)55; cynomolgus macaque embryo, GEO (GSE193007)56; RA-gastruloid, GEO (GSE208369)57; axial organoid, GEO (GSE220563)17; axioloid, GEO (GSE199576)18; and segmentoid, GEO (GSE195467)19. GEO series are accessible at https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/ and ArrayExpress experiments at https://www.ebi.ac.uk/biostudies/arrayexpress. The confocal and time-lapse datasets are large multichannel image series that are impractical to deposit in full; the measurement tables from which the quantitative imaging panels are plotted are provided in the code repository (Code availability). Raw imaging data, and any additional information required to reanalyse the data reported in this study, are available from the lead contact, S.R., on request; requests will be answered within 1 month and data shared by secure electronic file transfer without restriction. Source data are provided with this paper.

In a recent development, custom code for image analysis and for bulk RNA-seq and scRNA-seq analysis—including SMD feature selection, clustering and annotation, and the trunk morph–embryo correspondence analyses—is available under the MIT License at GitHub (https://github.com/stevenzwick/zwick-2026-trunk-morphogenesis) and archived at Zenodo (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22756590)58. Random seeds and exact parameters (intensity thresholds and gates, background offsets, local-threshold window sizes, Gaussian σ, histogram edges, clustering resolutions and curated gene lists) are provided in the repository.

According to recent reports, a, A detailed schematic of the workflow is shown: (i) Matrigel is microcontact printed onto the two-layered PDMS stamp (PDMS-ii) using a flat PDMS stamp (PDMS-i). (ii) A thin PDMS microwell array is peeled from the silicon master and overlaid on a glass coverslip. Taller PDMS sidewalls are plasma-bonded along two edges. (iii) Capillary water flow through the microchannels drives localized Matrigel transfer from stamp PDMS-ii onto the PDMS microwell layer at the contact interface. (iv) Cells are seeded onto the transferred Matrigel pattern, overlaid with a silanized coverslip atop the sidewalls, and cultured further with media and microwell-trapped beads. b, Photographs of the experimental setup corresponding to steps a(i–iii): coating the flat stamp (grey border, fourth column, top); PDMS-ii stamps with different patterns (blue border, first column); PDMS microwell layer with wells at different positions (red border, second column); aligned PDMS-ii stamp and PDMS microwell layer in contact (green border, third column); and the application of weight and water flow for transfer (green border, fourth column, bottom). MG, Matrigel; RT, room temperature.

a–d, Design of two-layer PDMS stamp and microwell substrate: a, upper-layer pattern used to print Matrigel features; b, lower-layer embedded microchannels (white denotes channel features); c, assembled two-layer PDMS stamp with a three-dimensional illustration of the assembled stamp below; d, alignment of stamp features and microwell layer, with 120 µm diameter microwells positioned at defined distances from pattern edges. Scale bars, 1 mm. e, Whole-chip images show humidified microcontact printing (HµCP) of Matrigel mixed with fluorescently conjugated BSA (cyan) onto PDMS microwell chip (brightfield, grey), using a four-square stamp pattern. Air bubbles beneath PDMS microwell layer and above glass coverslip are visible in brightfield images. Images are representative of 6 independent experiments (12 chips) with similar results. Scale bars, 1 mm. f, Whole-chip image reveals standard microcontact printing (µCP) of fluorescent BSA onto glass to validate stamp pattern from a. Image is representative of 2 independent experiments (5 chips) with similar results. Scale bar, 1 mm. g, Image shows pluripotent epithelial cysts formed 3 days after seeding on a PDMS microwell chip, using stamp pattern from a. A diversity of cyst arrangements, rather than the optimized hexagonal pattern with a central cyst as in Fig. 1, are used to show the flexibility of the approach. Image is representative of 79 independent experiments (145 chips) with similar results. Scale bar, 1 mm. h, Whole-chip epifluorescence image shows pluripotent cysts (DAPI, grey), well-trapped BMP4-coated beads (pseudocoloured red), and pSMAD1/5/9 immunofluorescence (pSMAD, green) 6 h after bead deposition. Image is representative of 6 independent experiments (13 chips) with similar results. Scale bar, 1 mm. i, Representative higher magnification images of cyst arrays with adjacent BMP beads and pSMAD1/5/9 immunofluorescence 6 h after bead deposition, from three independent experiments. (Top row) Five-cyst arrays with one or two beads, from chip in h. (Bottom left) Seven-cyst array with two beads, from an independent experiment. (Bottom right) Five-cyst array with three beads, from an independent experiment. Scale bars, 100 µm. j, (Left) Plot shows normalized pSMAD1/5/9 intensity (pSMAD/DAPI) versus distance from BMP bead, d, for all cysts from chip in h except cysts at centre of arrays (n = 201 cysts; light grey lines, individual cyst profiles; solid lines, mean; shaded areas, ±1 s.d.). (Right) pSMAD1/5/9 intensity in the bead-proximal epithelium of each cyst is plotted against the distance to the nearest bead, dmin, showing a negative correlation (red line, R2 = 0.624; n = 156 cysts) up to a distance of 635 µm, beyond which the intensity is low and uncorrelated (R2 = 0.061; n = 45 cysts). k, (Left) Normalized pSMAD1/5/9 is plotted against angle relative to bead direction (θ - θb) for cysts within responsive regime (d < 635 µm; n = 156 cysts). (Right) The direction of the pSMAD1/5/9 distribution, quantified by its first moment, is plotted as a function of the angle towards the nearest bead, θb (R2 = 0.17, n = 156 cysts). The correlation between pSMAD1/5/9 direction and bead angle is weaker than in Fig. 1f due to the overlapping influence of multiple BMP beads positioned near most cyst arrays in h.

a, (top) Live YFP and merged Brightfield (BF)–YFP images show hexagonally arranged cysts derived from the BMP4-T2A-Achilles reporter hPSC line 6 h after exposure to BMP4-coated beads (pseudocoloured red), with no detectable YFP signal. Images are from one experiment (36 cyst arrays). (bottom) Live images of the cysts from (top) 24 h after bead exposure show the presence of YFP (arrowhead) in some cells adjacent to beads. Images are from one experiment (2 cyst arrays). b, Plot of BMP4 read counts per million (CPM) from bulk RNA sequencing of pluripotent cysts at 0 h, 7 h, and 24 h after BMP bead exposure (n = 3 biologically independent samples per timepoint). Dots, individual samples; bars, mean; error bars, ±1 s.d. BMP5 expression was not detected in any of the samples. c, (left) Brightfield, DAPI (grey) and definitive endoderm marker SOX17 immunofluorescence (cyan) images show spatially arranged cysts after a 2-day exposure to the main experimental conditions, including BMP bead exposure, WNT-driven symmetry breaking, and Activin/Nodal signalling inhibitor A83-01 (above), or without A83-01 (below). Images are from one experiment per condition (with A83-01: 1 chip, 21 cyst arrays; without A83-01: 2 chips, 47 cyst arrays). (right) Bulk RNA-seq analysis of key endodermal genes in cysts under the same two conditions, with (green, n = 3 biologically independent samples) or without A83-01 (purple, n = 2 biologically independent samples). Dots, individual samples; bars, mean; error bars, ±1 s.d. A83-01 prevents endoderm differentiation in all protocols here (Extended Data Fig. 5b, Fig. 4, Supplementary Data 5). d, (left) Plot of DAPI-normalized SOX2 and TBXT intensity versus distance from central cyst of array (“anterior”). TBXT varies more with distance from anterior than distance from bead (Fig. 2c) due to A–P symmetry breaking from geometric cyst arrangement16,17 (Fig. 1b). Black arrow indicates the regime where both TBXT and SOX2 are high, corresponding to NMP differentiation (n = 210 biologically independent cysts; thin lines, individual cyst profiles; thick line, mean; shaded area, 95% confidence interval). (right) Pixel density plot of normalized SOX2 versus TBXT; percentages, fractions of pixels above and below the cutoffs. 28% of pixels are SOX2+ TBXT+, indicative of NMP-like expression. e, Brightfield, DAPI (grey), and TBXT immunofluorescence (cyan) images of three hexagonal cyst arrays without (left) or with a central cyst (right) on the same chip. In the absence of the central cyst, hexagonal cysts are prone to express TBXT on both their inward- and outward-facing poles (white arrowheads), indicating a lack of clear A-P polarity. With the central cyst present, TBXT expression is restricted to the outward-facing pole. Images are representative of 2 independent experiments (12 cyst arrays) with similar results. f, Brightfield and immunofluorescence images of cysts after 2 days of differentiation show FOXF1+ nascent lateral plate mesoderm (LPM, red) proximal to BMP4-coated beads (pseudocoloured red; red arrows top left, white arrows elsewhere), whereas FOXA2+ anterior mesoderm (magenta) and SOX2+ neural progenitors (yellow) are distant from beads. Cysts are from another chip of the same design (Extended Data Fig. 2a). Images are representative of 3 independent experiments with similar results. g, Pixel-density plots of FOXA2 versus FOXF1 (top) and SOX2 versus FOXF1 (bottom) immunofluorescence in day 2 cysts, indicating mutual exclusivity. Colour, log-scaled pixel density normalized to the 99th percentile of bin density; contours, equally spaced iso-density lines; dashed lines, positivity thresholds; percentages, fraction of pixels in each quadrant. n = 7 biologically independent cysts from 3 independent experiments. h, Images of cysts after 2 days of differentiation show FOXF1+ nascent LPM located proximally to BMP beads, FOXA2+ anterior mesoderm distant from beads, and TBXT+ mesoderm at posterior end of cysts. Images are representative of 5 independent experiments with similar results. i, Per-chip fraction of cysts containing FOXF1:Achilles+ cells, plotted as in Fig. 2e, for each condition: adjacent to a BMP bead (“Bead”), no bead (“No Bead”) and adjacent to a bead following BMPR1A knockdown (“KD”). Dots, one chip from each of four independent experiments; bars, mean; error bars, ±1 s.d. across experiments. n = 182 (“Bead”), 1,010 (“No Bead”) and 189 (“KD”) cysts scored in total (see Methods, “Fraction of FOXF1+ cysts”). j, BMPR1A CPM from bulk RNA-seq of cells following BMPR1A knockdown compared with a scrambled control (n = 3 biologically independent samples per condition). Dots, individual samples; bars, mean; error bars, ±1 s.d. Two-sided Welch’s t-test: t = −7.00, d.f. = 2.5, P = 0.010, mean difference −28.1 CPM (95% CI, −42.3 to −13.9). *P < 0.05. k, Quantification of pSMAD1/5/9 in cells at the edge following 30 min treatment with 10 ng ml−1 BMP4. BMPR1A knockdown cells show reduced pSMAD1/5/9 compared with SCRAMBLE control cells (n = 3 biologically independent samples per condition). Additional quantification at different time points and cell locations is provided in Supplementary Data 4. Dots, per-well medians; centre line, median; boxes, interquartile range; whiskers, extreme values within 1.5× interquartile range. l, Representative immunostaining images for the analysis in k: BMPR1A knockdown (top row) and SCRAMBLE (bottom row); knockdown cells (CFP, yellow, left), DAPI (middle), and pSMAD1/5/9 (cyan, right). Images are from one experiment (3 wells each). m, Images show two additional replicates of day 2 morphs as in Fig. 2f, showing the co-expression of BMP4:Achilles (green) and FOXF1:mScarlet3 (red). Images are representative of 3 independent experiments (13 chips) with similar results. n, Fluorescent RNA in situ hybridization images for BMP4 (green) and FOXF1 (red) transcripts show co-localization in a bead-adjacent cyst after 2 days of differentiation. Representative image from n = 6 biologically independent bead-adjacent cysts. o, Pixel-density plot of FOXF1 versus BMP4 in situ signal in the day 2 cyst shown in n. Colour, log-scaled pixel density normalized to its maximum; contours, equally spaced iso-density lines. The two signals are positively correlated (R2 = 0.646). Scale bars, 100 µm.

a, A schematic of trunk morph differentiation protocol is shown. hPSCs were seeded onto micropatterned PDMS microwell substrate on Day −3 in mTeSR Plus with 10 µM Y-27632. The next day, Y-27632 was removed from media conditions and Matrigel added to induce the formation of single lumen epithelial cysts. On Day 0, BMP4-coated beads were injected into microwells, and cyst differentiation was initiated in N2B27 with 8–10 µM CHIR99021, 0.1–0.15 µM A83-01, and 50 ng ml−1 NOGGIN. After 48 h, cysts were transferred to individual wells in N2B27 with Matrigel and cultured for 3–4 days before analysis. b, Box-and-whisker plots show length of trunk morphs at 0, 48, and 120 h of differentiation. The same n = 93 biologically independent trunk morph samples were tracked across all three time points. Centre line, median; boxes, 25th-75th percentile; whiskers, 1.5 × the interquartile range beyond the quartiles; dots, individual trunk morphs. c, (left) Box-and-whisker plots of trunk morph length on days 3, 4 and 5 without (red, n = 10 biologically independent trunk morph samples) or with the WNT-secretion inhibitor IWP3 (green, n = 8 biologically independent trunk morph samples), added after 48 h; each morph was tracked across all three time points. Centre line, median; boxes, 25th-75th percentile; whiskers, 1.5 × the interquartile range beyond the quartiles; dots, individual trunk morphs. Differences between conditions at each time point were assessed using two-sided Mann–Whitney U tests with Bonferroni correction for multiple comparisons; Hodges-Lehmann median differences are given with Bonferroni-adjusted (98.3%) confidence intervals. Day 3: U = 16, P = 0.103, −59 µm (−160 to 18). Day 4: U = 4, P = 1.6 × 10−3, −212 µm (−314 to −100). Day 5: U = 0, P = 1.4 × 10−4, −353 µm (−438 to −287). ns, P > 0.05; **, P < 0.01; ***, P < 0.001. (Right) Fluorescent RNA in situ hybridization images for WNT3A (left, green) and WNT5A (right, magenta) transcripts, together with brightfield imaging, show WNT ligand expression at the posterior end (n = 5 biologically independent trunk morph samples per probe, from 2 independent experiments). d, Representative epifluorescence images of trunk morphs after transient BMP4-bead exposure show FOXF1+ lateral plate mesoderm (cyan) bilaterally (left), unilaterally (middle), and posteriorly localized (right). Images are representative of 3 independent experiments (11 chips, 93 trunk morphs scored across all bead configurations) with similar results. e, Representative images of day 5 trunk morphs following transient exposure to medially positioned BMP4-coated beads. Posterior-restricted LPM was observed only at bead-cyst distances below 160 µm (5 of 12 morphs); all 9 trunk morphs with larger distances showed bilateral FOXF1. Images are from one experiment (3 chips, 21 trunk morphs). f-g, Representative images of trunk morphs exposed to (f) a unilateral bead or (g) two bilateral beads show unilateral or bilateral FOXF1, respectively. MESP2:mCherry is bilateral in all morphs. Images are representative of the same experiments and morphs as in d. h, Confocal images show DAPI (grey), MESP2:mCherry (red), phalloidin (grey), and FOXF1 (cyan) in a trunk morph. Single lumen, polarized somites (white arrows) are visible within the single focal plane. Images are representative of 2 independent experiments (2 trunk morphs) with similar results. i, Confocal images show DAPI (grey), phalloidin (grey), FOXC1 (cyan), and MESP2:mCherry (red) in a trunk morph. Single lumen, polarized somites (white arrows) are visible within the single focal plane. Images are representative of 2 independent experiments (4 trunk morphs) with similar results. j, Confocal images show DAPI (grey), phalloidin (grey), PAX3 (red), and SOX2 (yellow) in a trunk morph. Single lumen, polarized somites (white arrows) are visible in a 30-µm z-projection. Images are representative of 3 independent experiments (7 trunk morphs) with similar results. k, Confocal images at different z-planes (z = 330, 380, and 745 µm from the base) of trunk morph in Fig. 3h show DAPI (grey), FOXF1 (cyan), and MESP2:mCherry (red). As in many trunk morphs, somites (white arrows) are visible at specific confocal planes but are not apparent in the maximum z-projection shown in Fig. 3h. Scale bar, 100 µm.

Images are representative of 10 independent experiments (55 trunk morphs) with similar results. b, Epifluorescence images of day 5 trunk morphs without beads (left, three morphs; brightfield) or with a medial bead (right; DAPI, grey) show MESP2:mCherry (red; paraxial mesoderm), FOXA2 (green; axial mesoderm) and no SOX17 (magenta; endoderm). a, (Left) Hierarchically subclustered single-cell gene expression matrices are shown for cells originally assigned to somite clusters (“Early Somite”, “Mature Somite”) from trunk morphs without and with BMP bead exposure (see Supplementary Data 1, 5). (Top right) UMAP plots of 954 somite cell transcriptomes from trunk morphs without or with BMP bead exposure are shown, coloured by subcluster identity. (Bottom right) Stacked bar graphs show the fraction of each somite subcluster among somite cells from trunk morphs, without and with BMP bead exposure. b, Same as a, but for hierarchical subclustering of “Forebrain/Midbrain” cluster. n = 283 cells without beads; n = 263 cells with beads. c, Same as a but for cells from LPM and intermediate mesoderm (IM) clusters from BMP bead–exposed trunk morphs, revealing three distinct subpopulations: endothelial progenitors, cardiac-biased anterior trunk LPM, and posterior trunk LPM. Transfer Correspondent AUTHORITY Former Sky Sports and ESPN FC correspondent who specialises in global recruitment, contract negotiations, and high-velocity transfer breaking news. Enzo Maresca is unlikely to be sacked in the immediate future despite frustrations at Man City, sources have told Football Insider.

The boss has come under fire after a poor run of form of late, which has seen City win just one of their last seven games across all competitions in normal time.

Fans made their voices heard during the 1-1 draw against Fulham as they booed and jeered the players mid-game, calling for more intensity and urgency to their play.

However, as I revealed on the latest edition of Football Insider's Transfer Insider podcast, Maresca is under no pressure internally as Man City aim to turn their form around.

City have now dropped six points behind Arsenal in the Premier League title race, further raising concerns among the fans, but the board at the Etihad are remarked to be unfazed.

Instead, they are focusing on backing Maresca to bring success to Man City this season, and are not panicking about the situation they have found themselves in of late.

Former Man United assistant manager Mick Brown told Football Insider on 25 November that "alarm bells" are ringing over Maresca's future at Man City due to their recent form.

Their latest result at the Etihad has set alarm bells ringing both amongst the supporters and behind the scenes, and questions are now being asked about his role.

However, sources say Man City are not overly concerned about Maresca's performances and believe he will get them back on track before too long.

Speaking on the Transfer Insider podcast, I explained: "I don't think he's under immediate pressure, not from anybody within the club anyway.

"Results haven't been great of late, they've had just one win in their last seven games across all competitions, so obviously that brings its own pressure with it.

"The fans are not happy, obviously with that 1-1 draw against Fulham and then the Champions League draw against Napoli midweek.

"It’s an unenviable job trying to replace Pep Guardiola but you've to remember he's just new into the job himself so it's going to take time for to get his methods across and his ideas.

"So yeah, I think there's a bit of a frustration from supporters, but no pressure from inside this City camp really.".

Maresca's struggles and the frustrations among the Man City supporters have come as a result of a lack of intensity and energy amongst the players in his setup.

However, worse than that lack of intensity is their lack of defensive stability, which has left them open and raised concerns as a result of their poor structure at the back.

Brown told Football Insider on 26 November that Maresca has got to come down hard on his Man City players and instill some dicipline to their displays.

As things stand, there is a sense of freedom to City's style which can often lead to players, particularly defenders, being caught out of position and unable to get back.

Maresca has now told major changes will be needed on and off the pitch, with pressure growing on his position in the duout and fans already voicing their frustrations.

Peterborough United will be looking to pick up an vital victory when they welcome rivals Cambridge United to the Weston Homes Stadium on Saturday.

The hosts right now sit 22nd in the League One table, while the visitors are 11th.

Peterborough head into this local derby after ending a four-match winless run last weekend when they beat promotion chasers Plymouth Argyle 2-0.

Harry Ashfield opened the scoring in the first half, before Harry Leonard converted a penalty in stoppage-time to secure all three points.

The win was a welcome boost for Robbie Savage's side, who are fighting for survival and remain in the relegation zone with 13 points from 14 games.

However, they will be looking to carry the momentum of last weekend's win into Saturday's clash, with the Posh targeting back-to-back league victories for the first time since February.

It is also worth noting that Peterborough have a strong recent record against their rivals, having won their last five meetings across all competitions.

Cambridge, meanwhile, are without a win in their last five league games and suffered a disappointing 3-0 home defeat to league leaders Stockport County last Saturday.

Ollie Norwood broke the deadlock early in the second half with a stunning free kick, before Ethan Ennis doubled their lead and Gassan Ahadme scored an unfortunate own goal.

The defeat leaves the U's 11th with 21 points from 15 matches, having suffered just one defeat in their first 10 games before going five without a win.

Head coach Neil Harris has admitted his side have not been "tough to play against" in recent weeks and is keen for them to "get back to being that team".

Cambridge may be forced to make at least one change, with the availability of Kelland Watts in doubt after he was forced off against Stockport.

Patrick Bauer could replace Watts in defence, while Louis Appere is set to start up front with support from Zak Bradshaw and Ben Knight.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Liverpool are nicely on course to qualify directly for the Champions League round of 16 after their 3-0 win away to Club Brugge on Wednesday night.
  • The Reds’ 100% start to the league phase was ended by a 3-2 defeat to Fenerbahce earlier this month, but they responded to that setback in Istanbul with a thoroughly impressive victory against the Belgian side, with whom they were level on points prior to the match.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Liverpool are nicely on course to qualify directly for the Champions League round of 16 after their 3-0 win away to Club Brugge on Wednesday night.

The Reds’ 100% start to the league phase was ended by a 3-2 defeat to Fenerbahce earlier this month, but they responded to that setback in Istanbul with a thoroughly impressive victory against the Belgian side, with whom they were level on points prior to the match.

That result has left Andoni Iraola’s team fifth in the league phase standings with 12 points from a possible 15, with a top-eight finish seeing them bypass the bear pit of the knockout play-off round in February.

Now that we’re past the halfway mark of the league phase, the 36 Champions League clubs have a strong indication as to where they’re likely to finish, and what more needs to be done to achieve their targets.

In a recent development, want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

At present, Manchester City occupy the final position for automatic passage to the round of 16, with Enzo Maresca’s side on 10 points, averaging two per game.

That means the projected points tally required for a top-eight placing is 16, so Liverpool would need to aim for at least four points from their remaining three matches against Porto (home), Inter Milan (away) and Lens (home).

The two Anfield fixtures are against teams placed 22nd and 34th respectively, so the Reds would be fully expected to win both of those.

(Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images).

The visit to the San Siro is likely to be much tougher, but LFC beat Inter at the famous venue last season, and a repeat result would probably be enough to guarantee a top-eight finish with one game to spare.

That’d give Iraola the luxury of being able to rest key players for the concluding fixture against Lens, which falls between Premier League matches against Manchester United and Everton.

With Liverpool also still going strong in the Carabao Cup and plausibly making it to a two-legged semi-final in the opening weeks of 2027, any opportunity to rotate the squad in January must be embraced.

The picture can obviously change over the final three matchdays, but right now it seems probable that if the Reds beat Porto and get a result away to Inter, they could be effectively or even mathematically assured of a top-eight finish by the time they host Lens.

That objective is well within reach for Iraola’s side, and avoiding the play-off round in February is a must.

It has been revealed that arsenal have played six Premier League games this season and Bruno Guimarães has been a match-winning force in two of them. At this rate, he might justify his enormous £75m transfer fee by Christmas.

The Brazilian was not signed to be Arsenal’s super sub but that is the role he appears to be playing in these early days in north London. Against Leeds United here, as it was against Sunderland last month, he came off the bench when the champions were struggling. And as it was at Sunderland, he produced a thumping finish to put Arsenal on their way to three points.

In a recent development, liquid football from Arsenal 😮‍💨 Bruno Guimarães finishes off a well-worked team move! 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/WPrcA5ZrQ1 https://t.co/fbLJiaZbX5.

Industry observers note that this is the value of signing a 28-year-old with significant Premier League experience. As Arsenal laboured against an impressively organised and courageous Leeds side, Mikel Arteta knew that Guimarães was capable of coming into the game and adjusting to its demands. There has been no adaptation period required for Guimarães, who is fast becoming one of the most popular players in north London.

The finish, which put Arsenal 2-1 ahead at the Emirates Stadium, marked an emphatic conclusion to a fabulous passing sequence. Bukayo Saka, Martin Odegaard and Declan Rice all combined at speed before Guimarães charged on to Rice’s flick. “It was a beauty,” said Arteta of the goal. The move had actually begun at the feet of Guimarães a few moments earlier, when he nutmegged an opponent in style.

Sources indicate that the winning goal came just eight minutes after Riccardo Calafiori, Arsenal’s thrilling left-back/centre-forward hybrid, had pulled them level in the game. James Justin had struck for Leeds shortly after half-time, creating a horrible anxiety among the home fans here, and for much of the afternoon Daniel Farke’s side were the better team.

Leeds finally have their opener! 🤩 James Justin arrives at the back post to fire them ahead. 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/WPrcA5ZrQ1 https://t.co/ITjUMSlrG1.

Leeds, though, could not compete with Arsenal for depth. The arrival of Guimarães as a 63rd-minute substitute represented a flexing of Arteta’s managerial muscle, in his first match since signing a new long-term contract, and the Brazilian offered a moment of attacking quality that his opponents were unable to replicate.

It was actually the first competitive home game that Guimarães had played for Arsenal since his transfer from Newcastle United, as a result of a few niggles and the club’s unusual run of four consecutive away matches before the international break. The most recent of those was the 3-0 thrashing by Brighton, which was one of their worst defeats of the last few seasons.

Sources indicate that this gritty victory represented a necessary response to that defeat, even if the performance was far from dominant. “We had a point to prove,” remarked Arteta. “Something was touched in our identity against Brighton.”.

Guimarães, too, clearly felt that some wrongs needed to be made right. For all his brilliance in this game and against Sunderland, he had produced a horrible showing at the Amex Stadium a few weeks ago. “He was not at that level against Brighton,” said Arteta. “This is the level for Arsenal. Every week, every game, every minute, every action you have to be at that level. At Brighton, he wasn’t. Today, he was much better.”.

Leeds had not lost in their opening five Premier League matches of this season and it was easy to see why. They were willing to press Arsenal high up the pitch, taking risks and engaging in physical duels, and the strategy proved hugely effective for an hour.

Recent findings suggest that if they had been more precise in the final third, they could have been a few goals ahead by the time Justin converted Gabriel Gudmundsson’s left-wing cross after 55 minutes. Anton Stach, who was accidentally blocked by team-mate Jayden Bogle, and Gudmundsson both went close in the first half.

David Raya at his very best to deny Leeds the opener 😳 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/WPrcA5ZrQ1 https://t.co/hOB8RMapxw.

“I am heartbroken and gutted for my players,” remarked Farke. “They deserved to travel back with points today. The defeat has to do with the quality of the players they [Arsenal] could bring in. It is down to the mentality Mikel has created here that even on a tough day they find a way to win the game.”.

The early kick-off, the long international break, the slow start and the memories of the Brighton defeat made it a strange atmosphere at the Emirates. You would not have known they were the champions, based on the reaction of the fans to the first-half performance, but the achievements of last season clearly do not guarantee fervent support at all times.

Sources indicate that calafiori’s equaliser, which marked his fifth goal involvement in 10 games for club and country this season, changed the momentum of the game. The Italian is such an unusual player but this was a simple goal, converted from close range after Ben White had headed the ball back across the penalty area. “The energy changed immediately,” said Arteta.

Before the game we talked about two things, the challenge ahead against a team that had not lost in the Premier League. They full deserved to be where they are and it was going to be really tough. The second was to restore our identity and be ourselves again.

We weren’t pleased with our performance against Brighton and we wanted to put it right. But the context is that this was a difficult one [opponent]. But we reacted in a way that was unique and made it so special.

According to recent reports, when you play at 12.30 at home and you go one-nil down there’s a lot to do. You have to restore a lot of things. Energy is one of them. We had an incredible response. The crowd changed. You could see it.

In a recent development, we brought a lot of leadership on [with his three subs]. We brought goal threat, to win duels, people who can play forward and penetrate against their high press.

The timing, movement and execution of it [the winning goal], yes, it was a beauty.

Unbelievable. Against Brighton we were not at the level. This was all about bouncing back. This is my first official game at home. Great finish, I am very happy. My job if on the bench is to give a headache to the manager.

I have been proving myself in the Premier League but it was notable for me today.

As worrying as the result was at the Amex, Arsenal still created a shedload of chances and last season they were the one club that battered Leeds in both games – first early in the season when they were playing four at the back and before Dominic Calvert-Lewin, a late signing, was fully fit, and then later after they had successfully switched to a “base formation” of three centre-backs and the tactical flexibility that allowed.

In a recent development, it was a 5-0 tanking in August and 4-0 in January, so to say Leeds travel to a ground at which they have never won more in hope than expectation would be as true as much as it is hackneyed. Adding to a sense of foreboding and thanks to Opta’s excellent Jonny Cooper, we also have to take into account the fact that Leeds, floodlight kings, have not won a Premier League match kicking off before 3pm since August 2022 and have not won a match in London since beating Brentford in May that year to save themselves from relegation. Brighton are considering terminating Harry Howell's loan deal at Leicester City, sources have told Football Insider.

The 18-year-old joined the Foxes on a season-long loan deal during the summer, but has since started just two of his 13 appearances across all competitions under Russell Martin.

Brighton had hoped to see the attacking midfielder play more regularly, and are now considering recalling him from his loan with a view to another loan move in January.

A number of clubs in the Football League have expressed an interest in the England Under-19 international, and would be willing to take him in for the rest of the season.

Brighton have now been left with a difficult decision to make, with discussions underway behind the scenes about their next steps and what's best for Howell's future.

Leicester have given the teenager opportunities to perform in League One, but a lack of regular starts and the club's turbulent form may not be the best platform for him.

Brighton agreed to send Howell on loan during the summer as they were keen for him to continue his development by playing regular senior football at a high level.

The teenager has featured regularly for Leicester, but largely as an option from the bench, sparking concerns about the Seagulls' long-term plans for their young star.

Howell remains extremely highly regarded, not just at the Amex but within English football, having made seven senior appearances for Brighton before his loan move.

Now, clubs are said to be queuing up for his signature and could swoop if Brighton decide to pull the plug on his loan spell at the King Power Stadium.

Leiecester will surely be reluctant to lose a player who has featured heavily under Martin's guidance, but unless his situation changes between now and January, he could return to Brighton.

That would then allow the Seagulls to assess their other options, with a move to another EFL club most likely, as they aim for him to start regularly at a high level.

Howell is not the only player who could be on his way out of Leicester City in January, as the club are at risk of losing key players after their slow start to the season.

The Foxes presently sit seventh in the League One table, nine points shy of top spot, and alongside their first-team stars, some of their best young players could be tempted away.

Football Insider revealed on 25 November that Leeds United and Brentford are both plotting potential moves to sign Bismark Owusu in January.

The 18-year-old winger has impressed for the Foxes U18 side so far this term and is being tracked by multiple Premier League clubs as a result.

European outfits Parma, Utrecht and Copenhagen are also paying close attention to the starlet's progress, and could potentially launch a move for him this winter.

Alisson Becker made Champions League history in Liverpool’s win over Club Brugge

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Alisson Becker made Champions League history in Liverpool’s 3-0 win over Club Brugge on Wednesday night.
  • The Reds’ number 1 didn’t have his best outing in his previous European game, committing a costly error in the 3-2 defeat to Fenerbahce earlier this month, but he’s been in terrific form since that aberration in Istanbul.
  • He gave one of his best-ever performances in the recent victory at Crystal Palace and has followed that up with consecutive clean sheets against Manchester United and Club Brugge.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Alisson Becker made Champions League history in Liverpool’s 3-0 win over Club Brugge on Wednesday night.

The Reds’ number 1 didn’t have his best outing in his previous European game, committing a costly error in the 3-2 defeat to Fenerbahce earlier this month, but he’s been in terrific form since that aberration in Istanbul.

He gave one of his best-ever performances in the recent victory at Crystal Palace and has followed that up with consecutive clean sheets against Manchester United and Club Brugge.

Not only did he achieve a shutout in Belgium, he also claimed an assist for Alexander Isak’s second goal, with his long kickout finding the Swedish striker, who shrugged off the challenge of Brandon Mechele before finishing neatly past Yann Sommer.

As noted by liverpoolfc.com, Alisson became the first Liverpool goalkeeper to record an assist in the Champions League, with that being the fourth goal he’s set up during his time with the Reds.

It also puts him level with Pepe Reina and Bruce Grobbelaar for assists with LFC, and the Brazilian has achieved it in fewer games than those two.

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

Liverpool fans are no strangers to seeing their number 1 set up an attacking teammate to score, having done so for Mo Salah on three occasions, including the memorable clincher at home to Man United in January 2020.

We’ve even been fortunate enough to see Alisson get on the scoresheet himself with that famous stoppage-time winner against West Brom in May 2021 when Champions League qualification was in the balance.

The assist for Isak was a nice bonus to go along with another strong outing in terms of his core goalkeeping duties, having pulled off a terrific save to deny Felix Lemarechal when the score was 1-0 in the second half and Club Brugge were pushing hard for an equaliser.

As it stands, this’ll be the Brazilian’s final season as a Liverpool player, with his current contract due to expire next June, although his agent is reportedly in talks with club chiefs over a prospective extension.

Considering his ongoing importance to the Reds, we hope and pray that Alisson (still only 34) will agree to stay on for at least another year or two – possibly time enough for him to add more assists to his tally!

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Carter White | 26 Nov 2026 12:22, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 20:18.
  • Both aiming to halt their respective rotten runs of second-tier form, Millwall and Burnley lock horns at The Den in search of much-needed Championship points on Saturday afternoon.
  • The Lions were sentenced to another loss by promotion-chasing Stoke City earlier in the week, whilst the Clarets claimed an unwanted record in their 2-0 home defeat by Birmingham City.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Carter White | 26 Nov 2026 12:22, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 20:18.

Both aiming to halt their respective rotten runs of second-tier form, Millwall and Burnley lock horns at The Den in search of much-needed Championship points on Saturday afternoon.

The Lions were sentenced to another loss by promotion-chasing Stoke City earlier in the week, whilst the Clarets claimed an unwanted record in their 2-0 home defeat by Birmingham City.

After suffering just four Championship away defeats last season on their way to a third-placed finish, Millwall picked up their sixth loss on the road in 2026-27 at Stoke on Wednesday night.

The Lions extended their losing run to four consecutive matches following a lacklustre first-half display at the bet365 Stadium, where in-form striker George Hirst bagged a game-clinching brace for the hosts.

Winning just one of their past eight second-tier matches (D1 L6), Alex Neil's side have plummeted down to 18th spot in the Championship standings, a mammoth nine points behind the current top-eight pace.

Following four straight losses on the road, Millwall are in desperate need of some home comforts this weekend; however, the Lions have enjoyed victory in just one of their past six (D2 L3) competitive contests at The Den.

One of a multitude of problems facing head coach Neil ahead of a hectic festive period, the South Londoners are struggling in attack since the summer departure of Femi Azeez, scoring only once across their past four matches.

Whilst Millwall are experiencing a saddening fall from grace relative to last season, Saturday's visitors Burnley are in the midst of a full-blown crisis, with the recently-relegated side at the moment sleepwalking towards League One.

A 2-0 defeat by Birmingham at Turf Moor on Wednesday night made it 24 consecutive home league fixtures without a win for the Clarets - the longest such streak in the history of English football.

Despite this, head coach Fabio Celestini opted for the glass-half-full approach during his post-match media duties, insisting that Burnley bested Blues outside of the two boxes during the Lancashire loss.

The optimistic Swiss boss needs to increase his side's effectiveness in the decisive moments to avoid the same fate as Nicky Hayen, though, as the Clarets are winless in their opening five matches (D3 L2) with the 51-year-old at the helm.

Joining Premier League strugglers Manchester United on just the single league victory so far this season, Burnley are currently occupying 23rd position in the Championship rankings, four points from safety.

After accusing a number of his players of "not taking part in the game" at Stoke on Wednesday, it is safe to say that Millwall boss Neil is planning changes to his XI this weekend.

That indirect jab was likely commenting on the displays of Milhailo Ivanovic, Tairyk Arconte and Jenson Metcalfe, with the trio replaced at half time.

Derek Mazou-Sacko will start in the middle of the park, and influential Belgian Casper de Norre is set to return to the matchday squad.

Zak Sturge's absence reduces the hosts' options at left-back, with the 22-year-old picking up a straight red card during the defeat by Queens Park Rangers last Saturday.

Burnley also have a suspended player for this weekend's clash, with Wales international Connor Roberts out of action following his dismissal at Cardiff City on November 7.

The Clarets could make attacking alterations after firing a blank against Birmingham, with Marcus Edwards and Jamie Vardy pushing for starts.

Millwall possible starting lineup:.

Jensen; Osei-Tutu, Taylor, Cooper, Doughty; Kelly, Mazou-Sacko; Sykes, Neghli, Lisbie; Dykes.

Burnley possible starting lineup:.

Weiss; Walker, Alleyne, Julio, Pires; Cullen, Raghouber; Ramazani, Ramsey, Amdouni; Vardy.

After a soft display at Turf Moor earlier in the week, it is hard to imagine Burnley coping with the physical challenge posed by a trip to The Den.

Millwall were much-improved in the second half at Stoke and should be relatively confident of putting their relegation-threatened visitors to the sword.

Manchester United's chief executive Omar Berrada and sporting director Jason Wilcox are both under the threat of being replaced at Old Trafford.

That is according to former Everton chief executive Keith Wyness, speaking exclusively to Football Insider, who believes that the duo are part of a group of "three or four" boardroom figures facing uncertain futures.

Berrada recently conducted an interview with Sky Sports where he lifted the lid on the decision to replace Michael Carrick with Mauricio Pochettino, and also opened up on the club's power to spend moving forward.

However, Wyness believes that the interview hasn't had the desired effect for Berrada and has instead only placed further scrutiny on his position.

The 48-year-old suggested that the club hierarchy feel that United's squad was fundamentally improved ahead of this season, despite recent results suggesting otherwise.

Football Insider also recently revealed that Pochettino is keen to see Wilcox replaced as sporting director, as he is not convinced by his work for the club so far.

Everton’s former chief Wyness – who served as CEO at Goodison Park between 2004 and 2009 and now runs a football consultancy business advising elite clubs – believes that Berrada and Wilcox are both "in flux" at United at the moment.

The pair are both occupying roles that have seen changes in personnel regularly at Old Trafford in recent years, and also have their own futures under scrutiny right now.

Speaking on the latest edition of Football Insider's Inside Track podcast, Wyness was keen to point out that the squad has never been the problem for United.

"Look, the Man United story is incredible in terms of the scale and the attention it's getting as well," he stated.

"But I've got a funny idea about this in the sense that it's not to me that the squad is the problem. To me, the squad is the symptom of the bigger problem that is above the football management side.

According to recent reports, "Obviously, recruitment's not been great. That's proven with the results. But it's a symptom.

It has been revealed that "So there are three or four probably top positions, including those of Berrada and Wilcox that are in flux right now. I mean, there's intense scrutiny on them.

"And for Berrada himself, I don't know if that Sky interview helped that much.".

Wyness told Football Insider earlier this week that United have a hugely limited chance of signing Newcastle left-back Lewis Hall any time soon.

The boardroom expert believes that the Red Devils have no chance of "unsettling" the England international and convincing him to leave Tyneside.

Wyness outlined that players are now aware that United are not what they once were as a club, and are thinking twice before joining them.

He believes that Newcastle is the best place for Hall right now, and does not feel that a move to Old Trafford would provide any benefit for him.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Lewis Blain | 26 Nov 2026 12:28.

Manchester United have been handed a potential boost in their pursuit of Sporting CP left-back Maxi Araujo, who is reportedly keen on a move to Old Trafford.

The Uruguay international caught the attention of United officials during Wednesday's 2-2 draw in Lisbon, having been monitored by the club for several months.

However, a potential January deal could prove difficult given the asking price and Mauricio Pochettino's limited transfer budget.

According to Sport Witness, a source close to the situation has indicated that Araujo 'wants to join' United, with mutual appreciation between the player and the Premier League outfit.

United first showed interest in the 26-year-old earlier this year but failed to strengthen at left-back during the summer. Araujo subsequently extended his Sporting contract until 2030, which includes an €80m (£67m) release clause.

However, it's believed a fee closer to £50m could actually be enough to secure his services in the January transfer window, despite his new contract and substantial salary in Portugal.

United officials reportedly watched him closely during Wednesday's Champions League meeting, with Araujo playing the full 90 minutes.

The left-back has made 15 appearances this season and is viewed as a potential solution to United's problems in the position.

It has been revealed that luke Shaw has missed the last eight matches with a muscle injury, while youngster Harry Amass is also among the club's recognised options. Both players have contracts expiring in 2027, adding further uncertainty to the position.

Araujo's performance against United offered Pochettino an opportunity to assess a potential transfer target at close quarters.

Operating in an advanced left wing-back role, the Uruguayan registered two shots, created one chance, won three fouls and completed six progressive passes. He also made six defensive contributions, including three interceptions, per Sofascore.

It was not necessarily a spectacular individual display, but his all-round contribution attracted praise from the Portuguese press and demonstrated the qualities United could benefit from on the left flank.

Araujo could provide the attacking thrust and defensive work rate required to solve a problem position, although the financial implications are significant.

A reported £50m asking price would represent a sizeable investment, particularly with United believed to have less than that available for multiple positions in January.

Pochettino may be impressed by what he saw in Lisbon, but convincing the hierarchy to spend such a large proportion of their budget on one full-back could be difficult when central defence and striker reinforcements are also needed.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Inside the corridors of power at Manchester United, there is not the same appetite for a January splurge as there is among the club's fanbase.
  • While the winter transfer window brings hope for supporters desperate to see the mistakes of the summer rectified, United's decision-makers are anticipating a far more modest outlay.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By NATHAN SALT - FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 21:00 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 21:00 EST, 24 November 2026.

Inside the corridors of power at Manchester United, there is not the same appetite for a January splurge as there is among the club's fanbase.

While the winter transfer window brings hope for supporters desperate to see the mistakes of the summer rectified, United's decision-makers are anticipating a far more modest outlay.

As exclusively revealed by Daily Mail Sport, United strategy to spend less than £50million, with two additions targeted, one of which could be on loan.

Should United, currently 19th, remain in the bottom three by the time the window opens on January 1, there is a slim chance they go big in a desperate bid to guarantee their Premier League status.

But for now, the watchword inside United is discipline, and that means any recruitment will have to be more creative than ever before.

Here Daily Mail Sport looks at the transfer landscape and assesses eight players – a mix of Premier League proven and some lesser-known quantities – who could fit United’s needs AND their budget….

Mauricio Pochettino needs recruits in January - although Man United's budget being below £50m won't help his cause.

Brentford centre back Nathan Collins is one of United's top targets, but he won't be available on the cheap.

Position: Centre back, Age: 25, Club: Brentford.

In a recent development, signing Premier League proven players is absolutely the preference of the United hierarchy, as evidenced by their recent business. Six of their past eight arrivals joined with experience in the division under their belt.

Sources indicate that collins is one of the club’s top targets for the winter window. The 25-year-old Brentford captain would bring leadership, an aerial presence and is comfortable as a ball carrier from the back, which Pochettino values.

Collins is seen as having many of the same attributes that Harry Maguire has brought to United over the years. And while he is not a flash name, he is viewed as a player that can immediately deliver some solidity.

Highly durable and a threat at set-pieces, Brentford won’t be willing to part with their captain, who is under contract until 2029, on the cheap.

Signing Collins would eat up most of the budget – but United are not deterred.

Position: Left back, Age: 25, Club: Man City.

United made a late play to land the Algerian on loan in January, only for City to tell them they would only sanction a permanent exit. In the end, time ran out and Ait-Nouri stayed put.

Industry observers note that he has started just one game in all competitions under Enzo Maresca and is yet to feature at all in the Premier League this season. His situation is unlikely to improve in the near future, either.

A loan with an obligation to buy could suit all parties here, even if sending Ait-Nouri to their fiercest rivals may be difficult for City to stomach.

In a recent development, rayan Ait-Nouri (right) has fallen out of favour under Enzo Maresca and is yet to play a minute in the Premier League this season. Could he make a move across Manchester?

Position: Left back, Age: 27, Club: Crystal Palace.

An intriguing option given United have been keeping tabs on Mitchell for over a year.

Palace are quite secretive when it comes to Mitchell – they kept his last contract extension under wraps – but as it stands, his deal is set to expire at the end of the season.

Mitchell has the stamina to cope with Pochettino’s style of play and what he lacks in end product, he makes up for with his relentless pressing and recovery pace. The same is true of Fulham's Calvin Bassey, but sources are increasingly sceptical about United's chances of signing him in January.

Industry observers note that for all of Palace’s struggles, Mitchell is proven at this level and would likely hit the ground running. The fact United are not his only suitor is a sign they aren’t straying down a blind alley.

With the 27-year-old’s contract yet to be extended and massive clubs sniffing around, he could prove to be this January’s Marc Guehi should United nip in ahead of Liverpool, with Reds boss Andoni Iraola also keen.

Tyrick Mitchell has the stamina to cope with Pochettino’s style of play and what he lacks in end product, he makes up for with his relentless pressing and recovery pace.

Position: Forward, Age: 29, Club: Tottenham.

Out of favour under Roberto De Zerbi, Richarlison could help Tottenham Hotspur, Manchester United and himself in one fell swoop.

According to recent reports, in the summer, Spurs were looking for £20m for the Brazilian. Now the feeling is they would take a figure below £10m – some sources think £7m may suffice – to move on a player who has been kicking his heels since playing for the Under 21s away to Cheltenham Town in October.

Sources indicate that richarlison saw summer offers from Everton, Trabzonspor and Vasco da Gama fall through for various reasons and with United desperate to bolster their front line, this one could suit all parties. Richarlison is a strong presser from the front, versatile and better in the air than he is perhaps given credit for. He’s also no stranger to football's dark arts, something Pochettino appreciates.

The 29-year-old would offer a greater goal threat than Joshua Zirkzee, who saw moves of his own collapse in the summer, and showed last season what a threat he can be, scoring 11 league goals.

Spurs just want him out of the building and while that is normally a red flag, United need all the help they can get in a difficult market.

Richarlison is available for a bargain fee in January - even if he comes with some red flags attached.

Position: Centre back, Age: 28, Club: AC Milan.

United have rarely gone to the continent for recruits in recent seasons. But their limited budget makes Premier League players extremely difficult to acquire.

One option who might be available for a bargain fee is AC Milan's Fikayo Tomori, who is out of contract in the summer. The expectation in Milan is that Tomori will be moved on in January, allowing former United boss Ruben Amorim to add to his defence.

According to recent reports, tomori was initally frozen out by Amorim – he’d have a good ice-breaker should he pitch up at United! – and was even stripped of a squad number, before he was gradually reintroduced.

The England international has started just four games this season – only two in the league – and while Tomori has limitations in the air, he would bring Premier League experience and a level of leadership that is sorely lacking. His ability to bring the ball out and into midfield would make him a regular starter in Manchester.

When Milan won Serie A in 2022, Tomori was aggressive in his press and showed he could play on either side as a centre back, and also slot in at right back when required.

According to recent reports, milan want to sell him, United need defensive reinforcements, and a cut-price deal suits everyone. This one is a no-brainer, thanks to Amorim of all people.

Fikayo Tomori looks set to move on from AC Milan in January with former United boss Ruben Amorim keen to shuffle his defensive pack.

Position: Left back/centre back, Age: 29, Club: Stuttgart.

An experienced option that could cover multiple positions across the back line, Mittelstadt would prove really shrewd business.

Under contract until 2028, the player has not agitated for a move but sources in Germany have indicated no extension talks are underway at this stage.

Stuttgart are eighth in the Bundesliga and should European football start to look out of reach, a sale of someone like Mittelstadt may become a necessity.

United should look at him even though his resale value would be limited, as he would immediately bring experience and quality. Mittelstadt, who was Germany's first-choice left back at Euro 2024, is a proactive defender that doesn’t shirk challenges and his durability means United could count on him from the off – notable given their lack of high-quality options at left back.

Signing Mittelstadt would go against everything the club's executives want to do – but they showed by bringing in the 29-year-old Youri Tielemans in the summer that they are prepared to make exceptions on some older players.

Germany international Maximilian Mittelstadt (right) would add quality at full back.

Position: Left back, Age: 23, Club: Real Madrid.

Carreras should never have been allowed to leave United, but now comes a chance to rectify the mistake the club made in letting him go two-and-a-half years ago.

The 23-year-old has not been a regular starter under Jose Mourinho at Real Madrid and a player of his undoubted quality won't be happy with that state of affairs.

Real don’t need to cut their losses on a young player who is contracted through to 2031, which is exactly why Pochettino should go to Mourinho and see if he can take Carreras on loan for the rest of the season.

He is a better creator of chances than Patrick Dorgu or Luke Shaw and while Dorgu offers greater threat in the final third, Carreras feels a more well-rounded option at left back that is a better match-up against the league’s top wingers.

Carreras needs regular starts to develop and here is a chance for Mourinho to do his former side a favour when they are cash-strapped.

United made a mistake in letting Alvaro Carreras (right) go in 2024 - now it is time to rectify it.

Folarin Balogun forged a strong connection with Pochettino with the US national team and looks set to leave Monaco in the near future.

Position: Forward, Age: 25, Club: Monaco.

A striker that looked bound for Everton until a last-minute, deadline-day U-turn in the summer, it is widely known among recruitment staff that Balogun is available in January.

The Arsenal academy graduate has worked under Pochettino extensively with the US national team and, having had a reduced role at Monaco since the botched Everton move, a fresh start under a manager who knows how to get the best out of him would suit everyone.

‘There were just floods (of tears) from many people, but it's bound to happen,’ said Balogun when Pochettino left the USA job. ‘We had a really close relationship, him, his staff and us as players. We were really connected. It was always going to be a sad goodbye for that reason.’.

Pochettino and Balogun's desire to reunite will be strong, but money could be an concern here. A loan with a conditional obligation to buy could be the best compromise, with incentives based on United's league position or Balogun's goals scored.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Fabrizio Romano has revealed that the Liverpool hierarchy are ‘delighted’ with the work that Andoni Iraola has done so far as head coach.

It’s been nearly six months since the Basque was appointed as Arne Slot’s successor in the Anfield dugout, and so far the trend on his watch has been largely positive.

The Reds sit fourth in the Premier League table (one point off second) and are on course to once again qualify directly for the Champions League round of 16, while also progressing to the quarter-finals of the Carabao Cup.

Including penalty shootouts, Iraola has won 12 of his first 18 games in charge, with just three defeats (two of which came in controversial circumstances against Arsenal and Manchester City).

In a video on his eponymous YouTube channel, Romano spoke of how highly Iraola’s work so far has been regarded at Liverpool, with the head coach already in discussions with club chiefs over transfer plans for 2027 and beyond.

The Italian noted: “They are already discussing with Andoni Iraola about future plans and what they want to do. They are delighted with the coach and the coach is delighted with the Liverpool project. [He has] very good connections with the players.”.

According to recent reports, want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

Without intending to denigrate the job that Slot did at Liverpool, it seems undeniable that the performance levels of a few players have improved exponentially under Iraola.

Sources indicate that alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz have both been thriving in recent weeks, while Alexis Mac Allister has been drastically rejuvenated since the end of last season. With all three of those on song, the Reds’ chances of success should improve considerably.

Iraola notably signed a two-year contract when he took the job at Anfield, which at first may seem a surprisingly short agreement, but it’s one which aligns with how he’s operated at previous clubs.

He’ll know from how dramatically Slot fell from grace in the space of a few months that a glowing reputation now could count for nothing by April or May if Liverpool were to endure a prolonged slump over the winter and into spring.

For now, though, the current head coach has breathed newly introduced life into a fan base which was hugely disenchanted towards the backend of last season, and that appears to be recognised by the club’s hierarchy as they give a firm seal of approval to the job that he’s done so far.

Hopefully Iraola continues in the same vein for the rest of this campaign and beyond!

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Liverpool may make a surprise move to sell out-of-favour midfielder Ryan Gravenberch in the upcoming January transfer window.

That is according to former Everton chief executive Keith Wyness, speaking exclusively to Football Insider, who believes that the Dutchman could potentially make a return to the Bundesliga.

Gravenberch only signed a latest deal at Anfield back in March, but has fallen to the fringes of the squad under Andoni Iraola in recent months.

Wyness believes that Liverpool may already “regret” their move to tie Gravenberch down long-term, and are likely to consider selling him within the next 12 months.

The 24-year-old has started just four Premier League games so far this term, and is now out injured having been left as an unused substitute for the defeat to Arsenal on 1 November.

Trey Nyoni’s emergence in the first-team squad hasn’t helped Gravenberch, who now has an extra body to compete with for game time in the midfield.

Everton’s former chief Wyness – who served as CEO at Goodison Park between 2004 and 2009 and now runs a football consultancy business advising elite clubs – believes that Liverpool are likely to look favourably at the chance to offload Gravenberch’s “expensive wages” as soon as possible.

The former Ajax starlet made 50 appearances in all competitions last season, but has found himself behind both Dominik Szoboszlai and Alexis Mac Allister in the pecking order this term, as well as Nyoni at times.

Speaking on the latest edition of Football Insider’s Inside Track podcast, Wyness explained that he expects movement in terms of Gravenberch’s future either in January or next summer.

It has been revealed that “I don't think it's the player having regret, I think it's Liverpool possibly having regret as to whether they signed him. That's the problem. It's a bet on the system and when you change manager you change systems,” he said.

“And when he was given that renewal, that's what they were thinking about at the time. I think it’s probably the club that are thinking maybe that was the wrong decision at that time.

Industry observers note that “He's on expensive wages. Unless there's a squad depth matter that means they don't want to move him on, I think they'll be looking to move him on to the Bundesliga as soon as they can do. That’s where I think the interest might be.

“I'd expect to see possible movement even as soon as January, or if not next summer.”.

Football Insider revealed on Thursday that Liverpool will explore a “very expensive” move for Bayern Munich’s Jamal Musiala next summer.

Recent reports have suggested that the attacking midfielder has a release clause that can be triggered from next summer, with Bayern understood to be worried about his future.

However, Musiala is continuing to suffer from a neurological issue that is causing him to have seizures during games and training sessions, and he has started just once in the Bundesliga so far this term.

Liverpool are prepared to launch a move for the 23-year-old starlet ahead of next season, but only if he can prove his fitness at the top level between now and then.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Darren Plant | 26 Nov 2026 12:37.

Preston North End play host to Norwich City on Saturday afternoon looking for the win that could move them outside of the relegation zone.

At a time when the home side sit in 22nd place in the Championship table, Norwich remain in 11th position despite their prolonged unbeaten streak.

While many questioned why Graham Alexander left a League One promotion bid with Bradford for a relegation scrap at Deepdale, the Preston legend is currently justifying his decision.

Seven points have been accumulated across the last three fixtures against Southampton, West Ham United and Cardiff City.

Preston had been heavy underdogs in all three contests, yet they came through that triple-header having conceded just the one goal.

Although Preston had to battle hard to earn a share of the spoils at West Ham on Saturday, they were ruthless in dispatching Cardiff by a 4-0 scoreline in South Wales three days later.

Despite remaining three points adrift of safety, confidence is growing at Preston ahead of facing one of the form teams in the division.

Such has been the upturn in Norwich's fortunes that they were disappointed to record a 1-1 draw at home to Queens Park Rangers in midweek.

Nevertheless, having won their previous five games, it extended their recent return to 16 points from a possible 18.

Philippe Clement's side remain with three points of sixth-placed Southampton, a position they will take having lost eight of their opening 11 league matches this season.

Norwich have scored 19 goals in eight away fixtures, the joint-best attacking record in the division, while they have won their most recent three contests away from Carrow Road.

Preston North End Championship form:.

Norwich City Championship form:.

Barring any fitness problems, Preston boss Alexander is expected to name the same starting lineup from the Cardiff game.

Preston were 4-0 ahead before substitutions were first made in the 77th minute, and the same players should keep their places.

The likes of Harry Clarke, Lewis Gibson and Liam Gibbs are all expected to remain sidelined.

Meanwhile, Kenny McLean, Anis Ben Slimane, Oscar Schwartau and Jovon Makama are all in contention for opportunities in the Norwich XI.

Jacob Wright, Paris Maghoma and Mathias Kvistgaarden could be the players to drop down to the substitutes' bench.

Preston North End possible starting lineup:.

Nicholls; Hughes, Lindsay, Offiah; Mills, Thompson, Docherty, Small; Devine, Moran; Burgzorg.

Norwich City possible starting lineup:.

Grimshaw; Stacey, Darling, McConville, Yongwa; Field, McLean; Brooks, Ven Slimane, Musaba; Makama.

Although Preston recorded the most eye-catching Championship result in midweek, it remains to be seen whether they can back that up against a team playing with Norwich's confidence. Therefore, we are backing the Canaries to come out on top, albeit in a match where Preston will continue to show their improvements under Alexander.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Lewis Blain | 26 Nov 2026 12:48.
  • Chelsea have joined Tottenham Hotspur in keeping tabs on emerging France international Sael Kumbedi, who is attracting growing interest from a host of Premier League clubs.
  • The 21-year-old defender has enjoyed a rapid rise in Germany, with his recent senior international breakthrough further enhancing his reputation.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Lewis Blain | 26 Nov 2026 12:48.

Chelsea have joined Tottenham Hotspur in keeping tabs on emerging France international Sael Kumbedi, who is attracting growing interest from a host of Premier League clubs.

The 21-year-old defender has enjoyed a rapid rise in Germany, with his recent senior international breakthrough further enhancing his reputation.

Xabi Alonso is among several managers who appear to be assessing the versatile VfL Wolfsburg defender ahead of a potential transfer.

The Blues, Tottenham and Fulham are all 'monitoring' Kumbedi, while City Football Group have also been tracking his progress throughout the campaign, according to TEAMtalk.

The right-back moved to Germany from Lyon in August 2025, initially joining Wolfsburg on loan before the Bundesliga club activated their €6m purchase option.

Despite Wolfsburg suffering relegation to Bundesliga 2, Kumbedi opted to remain with the club and help them pursue an immediate return to the German top-flight.

His decision has not prevented his reputation from growing, with Zinedine Zidane handing him his first senior France call-up earlier this month following an injury withdrawal from the squad.

Kumbedi made his international debut against Italy at San Siro on November 12th, becoming the first Bundesliga 2 player to receive a France senior call-up since David Trezeguet in 2007.

Chelsea's interest in Kumbedi could make sense given the uncertainty surrounding their options at right-back.

Reece James' injury problems have created a significant headache for Alonso, with Pedro Neto having been deployed in a wing-back role and centre-back Josh Acheampong also shifted out to the right.

Malo Gusto's uncertain future at Stamford Bridge is another potential consideration, leaving Chelsea with reasons to explore the market for a specialist defender capable of providing greater depth and versatility.

European scouts are reportedly impressed by his pace, athleticism and stamina, while his ability to operate on either flank further adds to his appeal.

That versatility is particularly attractive to a side like Chelsea, who are seeking defensive reinforcements in 2027, with the French gem's performances over the coming months likely to remain under close scrutiny.

However, the west London side are not alone in their interest, with top-flight rivals Spurs, Fulham and City also monitoring the Frenchman.

His international breakthrough could make competition for his signature increasingly fierce, but Chelsea's need for greater stability and depth on the right makes this a potential transfer worth watching.
